missing_algorithms: No protein structure prediction (alpha folding, homology modeling, or secondary structure prediction) — protein.py only computes primary sequence properties (MW, pI, hydrophobicity, composition)
No gene network analysis (co-expression, regulatory network inference, or gene-gene interaction modeling) — no module exists for network-level genomics
No metabolic pathway modeling (flux balance analysis, pathway enrichment, or metabolic network reconstruction) — no KEGG/PlantCyc pathway integration
No phylogenetic analysis or multiple sequence alignment (MSA) — variant.py and protein.py lack evolutionary context needed for conservation-based scoring
No gene prediction or ORF finding — no tool to identify coding regions in genomic DNA
No promoter/enhancer element prediction — regulatory element detection is absent
No RNA secondary structure prediction — relevant for gRNA efficiency and mRNA stability
No copy number variation (CNV) or structural variant (SV) detection beyond simple indels
No genome-wide association study (GWAS) or quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping support
No gene ontology (GO) enrichment or functional annotation pipeline
bottlenecks: CRISPR off-target scoring is O(n) per guide with no genome-wide index — cannot scale to whole-genome off-target search without a suffix array or BWT index
Variant effect prediction processes variants sequentially in predict_batch (list comprehension) — no parallelization for large VCF files
Allergenicity similarity calculation is O(n*m*k) where n=query length, m=db size, k=window size — will be slow for large allergen databases
Codon optimizer uses a single most-frequent codon per amino acid — no consideration of codon pair bias, mRNA secondary structure, or tRNA pool optimization
No caching of expensive computations (protein analysis, variant prediction) — repeated calls recompute from scratch
GFF3/GTF parsers load entire files into memory — no streaming parser for large genome annotations
No database or file-based persistence for analysis results — all in-memory only
benchmark_gaps: CRISPR efficiency_score uses a simple heuristic (GC content + poly-T penalty + G bonus) — not validated against established tools like CRISPRscan, CHOPCHOP, or Rule Set 2
CRISPR off_target_score is a placeholder heuristic (GC deviation + k-mer complexity) — no alignment-based off-target search (e.g., Bowtie/BWA integration) or CFD score calculation
Variant SIFT score is a binary conservative/radical classifier (0.7 or 0.1) — real SIFT uses position-specific scoring matrices from protein multiple sequence alignments
Variant PolyPhen score uses only charge and hydrophobicity — real PolyPhen-2 uses structural features (secondary structure, solvent accessibility, B-factor) plus sequence-based features
No benchmark dataset integration (ClinVar, dbSNP, gnomAD) — variant predictions cannot be validated against known pathogenic/benign variants
No ROC/AUC or precision/recall evaluation framework for any predictor — no quantitative performance metrics
Solubility predictor uses a simple weighted sum of 4 features — not benchmarked against experimental solubility databases (e.g., eSol, PROSO II)
Localization predictor uses regex patterns only — no SignalP/TargetP/DeepLoc integration or machine learning-based prediction
No cross-validation or holdout testing framework — all predictors are untested against independent datasets
Codon optimization uses only 3 species (rice, maize, wheat) — missing Arabidopsis, soybean, tomato, and other major crops
No integration with external tools or databases (UniProt, NCBI, Ensembl Plants, KEGG) — all data is hardcoded
No confidence intervals or uncertainty quantification on any prediction score
